# A. Quantile Prefix Sum

## How to find it

Alongside zero counts, store prefix sums of the zero subsequence at every wavelet level.

## Correctness

Whenever k passes the zero block, all those values are among the k smallest and their sum is added once. The remaining path ends at one equal value class supplying the final copies.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# B. Clamped Terrain

## How to find it

Maintain symmetric maximum and minimum beats metadata and push both inherited bounds.

## Correctness

Each fast upper or lower operation changes one extremal value class exactly. Recursive cases partition until every changed class is handled, while push preserves all ancestor clamps.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# C. Reversible String Hash

## How to find it

An implicit treap stores forward and reverse polynomial hashes; reversal swaps both children and hashes.

## Correctness

The in-order hash recurrence is exact after every pull. Lazy reversal produces the reverse sequence and swaps its two hashes, so equality is exactly the maintained palindrome certificate.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# D. Dynamic Forest Sum

## How to find it

Use path exposure exactly as for XOR, but store additive aggregates and point assignments.

## Correctness

Exposure selects exactly the represented path and splay pulls maintain its vertex sum, hence every query returns precisely those vertices once.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# E. Earliest Connection

## How to find it

Label each Kruskal reconstruction merge by its input edge index.

## Correctness

Two vertices first become connected at the merge represented by their reconstruction-tree LCA. If they have different final roots they never connect; identical vertices connect at time zero.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# F. Affine Forest Paths

## How to find it

Apply affine tags to an exposed path and compose a new tag after the pending old tag.

## Correctness

For a subtree of size s, `x -> ax+b` changes its sum to `a*sum+b*s`. Composition `new(old(x))` gives the stored multiplication and addition formulas, so delayed updates remain chronological.

## Complexity

`O((n+q) log n)` expected/amortized time and `O(n log sigma)` or `O(n)` structure memory, as appropriate.

# Contest-wide validation

Compare A with sorted slices and prefix sums, B with direct element clamps, C
with literal strings, D/F with BFS path reconstruction in an adjacency-list
forest, and E with replayed edge prefixes. Include all-equal values, empty
effective clamps, palindrome reversals, one-vertex paths, failed duplicate
links, and many edges sharing one threshold.

The reusable habit is to separate represented state from storage state:
wavelet partitions, treap rotations, splay preferred paths, and reconstruction
nodes are correct only insofar as their summaries preserve the original query
boundary.
